quest.title: Eight Locales Over Mountains and Seas
quest.description: You have not gone to see Ioroi of Chinju Forest for quite some time now. Perhaps it's time to pay the sealed king of bake-danuki a visit...

talks.objective: Head to Chinju Forest to visit Ioroi

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there, Ioroi!

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: Eeek! You saw through me? How did... Wait, no, this scent...

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: Ah, so it's you. It has been so long, I could not recognize your scent!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And you haven't changed at all, Ioroi — still scared of humans and stuck in a stone!

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: Mmm!? What do you mean by that?

choices.text: Hope your seal can be lifted soon.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Bah, it is but a human seal! If I were but to try harder...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: *cough*

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: #Well. Regardless, I see you have taken good care of the little ones. My little tanuki often say that they enjoy playing with their nice-smelling yellow-furred {F#Aunt}{M#Uncle}.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: And here I had thought that humans were all the same as that fellow who had us sealed — wicked and scary. But it seems that there are still some good eggs amongst you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right. Most of the people we've met are good people! You got sealed because you stole that comb...

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Hmph! And I've returned it! So if you ever meet that fellow who learned magic from Reizenbou, tell him to get me out of this stone!

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Mmph! When you get down to it, everything is that sneaky kitsune's fault...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Ioroi really complains like some old geezer, huh?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Well, he is quite old.)

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Well then, neither your hands nor legs are made of stone, so you've been to many places, surely?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup! We came right over the ocean, you know?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell Ioroi about your adventures in Mondstadt and Liyue.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: ...So, there are so many lands abroad. Very impressive.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: I have been subsisting off reports from the little tanuki all this while, and so do not know what the outside world is like.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Once upon a time, I stood at the summit of Mt. Yougou and saw a very, very high mountain on the other side of the ocean. It was possibly even taller than Mt. Yougou. I still wonder, even today, what that place was.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's gotta be Dragonspine, right?

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Mmmm, Dragonspine? Just thinking about that name makes my tummy feel cold. Goodness knows why that fellow wants to go there...

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: As I said earlier, you are fine folk, yes? So...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon can smell this request coming a mile away!

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Mmm! Even like this, I am still the Hidden Protector of the Grove, defender of Chinju Forest, and thusly appointed by Her Excellency herself! If I was not sealed in stone, I would certainly use an eight-tatami large...

choices.text: Alright then. What do you need help with?

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Though I cannot move on my own power, the little children can do so. As such, I would like to ask you to take the little tanuki out to train.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Take Kichiboushi with you. He has been quite eager to see you since the last time you played together — quite eager indeed!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's true. We can't understand what Kichiboushi says, so wouldn't traveling together be kinda tough?

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Impossible. We tanuki understand human speech by nature. It is you humans who do not speak ours.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? Is that how it is?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But as travel companions...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We'd like to chat as we travel, you know?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Just like Paimon does with {NICKNAME}!

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Mmph. Very well then. Now that I consider it, didn't someone once use our magic to make you some food?

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Now, I may look like this, but making you a "meal" that can allow you to understand Kichiboushi's speech is hardly impossible nonetheless.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Woo-hoo! Food!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Is it gonna taste good, though...

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Now, now, don't you underestimate my culinary prowess!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Although you can't be sure where Ioroi got it from...\nYou and Paimon have a feast that "looks very delicious" off Ioroi's stone tummy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, this is great!

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Of course. I am Ioroi, you know — the very same who once made Sashimi Platters out of mud balls and tanuki fur to utterly deceive the Four Oni of Ogata!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's awesome, Ioroi! But so, what did you make the meal we just had out of?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Some questions are best left unasked, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, forget it. Let's go find Kichiboushi and have a chat!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Ooh, Paimon knows what you mean, {NICKNAME}! Will there be treasure?

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Treasure? Why, of course! I am the chief of five hundred and five bake-danuki, after all! Not a single one of Inazuma's treasures has ever escaped my sight.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: In that case, what do you need help with?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right, we're super good at helping!

choices.text: From the direction you're referring to, that's probably Dragonspine.
Paimon means that we hope that your seal will soon be lifted.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there, Kichiboushi! Long time no see!

dialogues.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
dialogues.text: Mm! White Fur, Yellow Fur.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I guess "Yellow Fur" must be me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Who're you calling White Fur?

dialogues.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
dialogues.text: Mm, very strong. Can understand.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #I'm {NICKNAME}, and this is Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And you'd better remember that!

dialogues.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
dialogues.text: Squelch squelch Lavender Melon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? Lavender Melon? And what's "squelch squelch" supposed to mean?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, at least we can kinda-sorta communicate...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Kinda-sorta" is kinda-sorta right.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Whatever the case, {NICKNAME}, let's go back and see Ioroi again. We are taking Kichiboushi out on a long journey, after all.

dialogues.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
dialogues.text: Ioroi! Yey!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yey!

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: Mm! How goes it?

dialogues.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
dialogues.text: Mm! See White Fur, Yellow Fur, very happy. Lavender Melon Kapow!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Lavender Melon Kapow...

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: Hmm, quite the bright spark, aren't you?

dialogues.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
dialogues.text: Kapow!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, what does Lavender Melon Kapow mean again...?

dialogues.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
dialogues.text: Kapow is Kapow. Lavender Melon is Lavender Melon.

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: Well, it seems that communications have been established without any problems. Ah, mine "culinary" skills are as fine as ever!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nope, not at all! We can't understand a thing Kichiboushi's saying!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, Ioroi, here's the thing...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell Ioroi how the attempted interactions are going...

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Mmm, so that's how it is. Not to worry. It is because you are not yet used to Kichiboushi's aura.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Take it slow! The more used to his aura you are, the better you shall understand him!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How slow are we talking about here?

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Ah, hmm. Let me think about that...

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Eh! Whatever the case, do not be in a rush!

response.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
response.text: Rush no good.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You don't know either, do you?

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Hmph! I will have you know that I am Ioroi, the long-lived king of bake-danuki! I simply do not put such premiums on time as you humans do.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Even though he's spent most of his time sealed in that stone statue...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Then why can you speak to humans just fine, Ioroi?

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Mmph! Such impertinence! Rather, you should ask why you humans may speak to us.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Having lived as long and become as powerful as I have, I have had at least some interactions with humanity.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: A long, long time ago, I often spoke with tengu, kitsune, oni, youkai, and humans alike. And while human stories often concern themselves, at least half of them involve bake-danuki who transformed into humans.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Half of the remaining half are indeed about humans themselves, and the other half are about all the other youkai.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: But even in this half, a good half concern we tanuki, who clad ourselves in the guise of the other youkai. Then half again of the tanuki tales are those concerning me.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Mmph, as such, you may see that I am the greatest of them all. Naturally, speaking to you young ones is no tall order at all.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I get it. Five over sixteen to Ioroi, yes?

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Mm? What's "Five Over Sixteen"? Is it something that one may eat?

response.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
response.text: Sounds delicious. Want to eat.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}'s referring to the percentage of stories that you're involved in, Ioroi.

response.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
response.text: Ioroi. Powerful!

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Hah, why of course! You have much to learn from my powers, you do.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? Come to think of it, we're starting to get what Kichiboushi is saying, aren't we?

response.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
response.text: White Fur smart.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That might have been praise, but Paimon sure doesn't feel good about it.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Good, good. Then I leave this child in your hands. Take him to go see the world and train!

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Why, when I was but a young tanuki, I too went on a pilgrimage to eighteen sites in Inazuma along the trail of the great bake-danuki Tsukumo, never once straying from the tanuki paths — only thus did I reach my present stature.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? Is that why you were sealed in stone?

response.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
response.text: Mm-haha! Stone!

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Eh!? You too, Kichiboushi...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ahem! So, uh, back on topic! Where should we go first?

choices.text: There's that place Ioroi mentioned earlier...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh-huh! Dragonspine it is, then!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "If there's a mountain, we shall climb it" — ah, Paimon's been waiting for a chance to say something cool like that!

response.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
response.text: Mountain, there!

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: Oooh, that sounds cold... Don't let your tummy get cold now, Kichiboushi. You'll catch a cold otherwise, and if you do, you won't be able to perform using your belly drum.

response.speaker: Ioroi
response.text: #Also, remember to eat properly and follow {F#Aunt}{M#Uncle} Yellow Fur like a good boy.

response.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
response.text: #Understand! Following {F#Aunt}{M#Uncle} Yellow Fur!

choices.text: We'll take good care of Kichiboushi, don't worry.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Pleased to meet you, Kichiboushi!

response.speaker: "Kichiboushi"
response.text: Mm! No worry! Kichiboushi take care of you!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, looks like we're not completely getting through to him...

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: Through the power of the bake-danuki meal made by mine own hands, you, too, may speak to the little tanuki. Go, try having a chat with Kichiboushi.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We'll do that.

dialogues.speaker: Ioroi
dialogues.text: Go, then, go. I have all the time in the world to go nowhere, but it is not so with my little tanuki.
